signal_or_failure: $0 net sales across the whole 179-day 1994 stub while $52,000 of operating expense was incurred
magnitude: 0 USD of net sales; 52,000 USD of expense
what_it_demonstrated: That the first reported period was pure spend: no revenue line at all (filed as '--')
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the spend bought validation: equity ended the stub at $8,000 and working capital at $(16,000)
notes: Nominal 1994 dollars; audited and filed in 1997, so a retrospective filing on an in-window state.

signal_or_failure: About twelve months elapsed with no recorded revenue: 'for the period from inception through July 1995, the Company had no sales'
what_it_demonstrated: That the company carried a full year of pre-revenue burn
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That timing was immaterial: it contradicts the founding rhetoric 'when it's growing 2,300% a year, weeks are important', a figure absent from the filings
notes: U.1: 'through July 1995' can read as up to the start of July or through the end of July; on the second reading July 1995 itself recognised no sales.

signal_or_failure: FY1995 operating loss
what_it_demonstrated: Losses were the whole Stage-1 record: the first full trading year lost money at the operating line
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Causal size: quarterly data begins Q1-1996, so no in-year loss curve exists
notes: Net loss $(303,000); loss per $1 of net sales $(0.595), DERIVED 304/511.

signal_or_failure: Marketing and sales spend exceeded gross profit
magnitude: marketing 200,000 USD vs gross profit 102,000 USD
what_it_demonstrated: That growth in 1995 cost more than it earned, on the company's own audited lines
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That this was wasteful: no channel-level cost or attribution data exists
notes: Advertising inside that line was only $30,000, so paid acquisition was near-absent: the spend is people, catalogue and effort.

signal_or_failure: On the audited ratios no order size was profitable: ~19.96% gross margin against marketing at 39.1% of net sales
what_it_demonstrated: That the Stage-1 cost structure was arithmetically loss-making per dollar sold, without any hindsight
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Per-order loss: order counts and average order value were never disclosed, so the loss cannot be attributed to basket size
notes: Arithmetic: 0.1996 - 0.3914 = (0.1918). Margin would have needed ~79% at these ratios. Class ESTIMATE for the 79% figure, which is why it is stated as a bound and not a target.

signal_or_failure: Cumulative losses reached $107,000, ending the Subchapter S election
what_it_demonstrated: That the accumulated deficit consumed the company's tax status before it had sold anything
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That this was a planned milestone: the filing states no reason
notes: Note 1 Income Taxes. THE CUMULATIVE-DEFICIT CLAIM IN THIS CELL WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED per AUDIT 3 (HIGH): the audited accumulated deficit at 1995-12-31 is $248,000, filed at S-1 (orig.) l.3461 and repeated as the closing balance of the statement of stockholders' equity at l.3571 - not the $355,000 this row asserted. WHY THE TWO DIFFER: the two loss years do sum to 355 (52 + 303, orig. l.3540 and l.3567), but $107,000 of that was RECLASSIFIED TO COMMON STOCK when the Subchapter S election ended (equity statement l.3555; Note 1 l.3713-3716), so 52 + 303 - 107 = 248 = the filed deficit. $248,000 is NOT the cash the company burned either: pre-April-1995 losses passed through to the founder's personal return. The failure signal is unaffected in kind and only mildly reduced in magnitude: eleven people ended the first trading year owing $248,000 of cumulative losses, after consuming $284,000 of cash.

signal_or_failure: Only a fraction of the advertised catalogue was sourceable: up to 400,000 distributor-supplied titles against >1,000,000 advertised in-window
what_it_demonstrated: That supply, not demand, capped the core claim from month one
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: A 1995 measurement: the 400,000 and 350,000 ceilings are 1997 disclosures, and the 2.5 million figure must never be back-dated into Stage 1
evidence_class: FACT (1997 disclosure) + INFERENCE (applied to the 1995 offer)
notes: U.3; COR-04. Kaphan's gloss converts the claim into a listing: 'we did have a million titles. We didn't have a million books'.

signal_or_failure: Unfilled demand was disclosed: four to six weeks for the in-print remainder, two to six months out of print, and 'some titles may not be available at all'
what_it_demonstrated: That the availability promise ('If it's in print, it's in stock') had a disclosed hole
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: How big the hole was in 1995: no fill rate, back-order rate or unfillable-order rate was ever quantified
notes: The timing bands appear in a 1997 filing describing 1996-97 operations; no 1995 timing measurement exists.

signal_or_failure: Card acceptance was obtainable only on the founder's personal guarantee
what_it_demonstrated: That a two-person firm with $0 borrowings could only get payment rails by pledging personal credit
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Scale: guarantee amounts, caps, scope and merchant rate are all UNKNOWN
notes: U.18. The Seafirst guarantee ran about eight months before the company could sell anything, standing in for a balance sheet with $83,000 of payables growth.

signal_or_failure: No supplier protection: 'no long-term contracts or arrangements with any of its vendors' guaranteeing availability, payment terms or credit limits
what_it_demonstrated: That the entire supply leg ran on unguaranteed per-order terms - disclosed fragility, not hindsight
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That it failed in Stage 1: nothing in the record shows a Stage-1 supply breakdown, and the 1995 distributor share is undisclosed
notes: Present-tense wording across the audited period reaches 1995 as the company's own account; no distribution or publisher agreement is filed as an exhibit.

signal_or_failure: The supplier armed competitors: Ingram disclosed as helping others 'establish and operate online sites for booksellers'
what_it_demonstrated: That the sole scaling mechanism was also available to rivals
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any 1995 quantification: the 59% Ingram share of purchases is a FY1996 basis and the 1995 share is UNKNOWN
notes: Rule 1: 59% is barred from Stage-1 metrics; recorded here as the disclosed structural weakness only.

signal_or_failure: Sales tax collected only in Washington, with no reserve or quantified contingency
what_it_demonstrated: That the price advantage partly rested on an unsettled legal posture
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the exposure was zero: the notes' only contingency is the 1997 B&N suit, and other states 'may seek to impose' collection obligations
notes: Absence of a reserve evidences posture, not absence of exposure. *Quill* (1992) is background law with no evidenced Stage-1 nexus.

signal_or_failure: Single-site infrastructure: all hardware at one Seattle-area site, periodic interruptions, no redundant systems, no formal disaster-recovery plan, insufficient business-interruption insurance
what_it_demonstrated: That the whole trading capability of the company could fail at once
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That 1995 specifically looked like this: the disclosure is a 1997 filing describing 1995-96, so the 1995 application is an INFERENCE
notes: Consistent with $0 leasehold improvements at year end.

signal_or_failure: Accounting was not integrated with the transaction system, requiring 'a significant amount of manual effort'
what_it_demonstrated: That the back office was human: the automation surface was narrow
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the numbers are wrong: both separately-accessioned filings repeat this disclosure, which is why it counts as corroborated
notes: Disclosed in T01 AND T02, so independence is genuine here (unlike most S-1 echoes).

signal_or_failure: Card details were captured off-line (e-mail, telephone) per the filing, and by fax per the Nov-1995 press only; reject handling is undocumented; nine customer-service e-mail addresses served as the service desk
what_it_demonstrated: That payment ran through unsecured channels in a period with no card-security standard
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That fraud or chargebacks occurred or did not: rejects and chargebacks are disclosed nowhere for 1995
confidence: High (channels, filing) / Medium (fax, press) / UNKNOWN (defect rates)
notes: COR-13: the nine e-mail addresses are the S-1's, at orig. l.2174, and the toll-free line at l.2179-2180 — not the 1995-10-04 press release, which says only that customers order online and names no mailbox, toll-free, fax or e-mail ordering. 'Fax' occurs zero times in the ordering text of all three S-1 versions; it reaches Stage 1 only via Knight Ridder, Nov 1995 (S0612).

signal_or_failure: Manual choke points in the 'automated' store: special-order sourcing, price requotes needing customer approval, packing by staff, a ten-book wholesaler minimum beaten by hand
what_it_demonstrated: That per-order economics were labour-laden
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Magnitude: no labour-hour, error or rework measurement exists. The lichen-book workaround is a 1999/2000 founder recollection
notes: Order-splitting software is disclosed; what it could not route went to an internal special-order group.

signal_or_failure: No 1995 evidence of repeat purchase exists anywhere in the record
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing about retention in Stage 1
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That customers returned: '>40%' is a March-1997 statement about 1997 orders; 60% (May-1996) and 44% (Jan-1997) are company figures on unpublished definitions
notes: Stage-1 demand demonstrates first purchase only; cohorts, retention and acquisition cost are absent.

signal_or_failure: Order counts, average order value, units per order and cost per order were never disclosed
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing: unit economics are structurally unmeasurable for 1995
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any per-order claim, favourable or unfavourable
notes: Quarterly disclosure begins Q1-1996, so every 1995 weekly or monthly curve in the literature is non-primary by construction.

signal_or_failure: Management-resource strain: 11 employees, no VP Engineering before March 1997, disclosed difficulty attracting qualified developers
what_it_demonstrated: That the company named resource strain as its own risk in-window
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That it bound the firm: contractors and temps were used but never quantified
notes: Hiring difficulty is corroborated by Kaphan's account; 'four employees in the garage' is memoir and conflicts with the filed 11.

signal_or_failure: The company's own filing warned that 'growth rates experienced to date are not sustainable'
what_it_demonstrated: That the fragility of the growth story was visible at the time, to the company
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: A runway: the implied 3.5-year figure (DERIVED 996/284) is arithmetic on one year of burn, not a plan
notes: Recorded so no reader mistakes the 1995 growth for a demonstrated trend.

signal_or_failure: FAILED TRACING: the '2,300 percent a year' Web-growth statistic that supposedly drove the founding
what_it_demonstrated: That the figure was used publicly by the founder from 1997 journalism onward
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That any contemporary source contained it: the only documented underlying data are a February-1994 newsletter's growth FACTORS (x2,057, x2,560), restated as a rate by a 2013 book
confidence: High (that it is unsupported) / Medium (on what he read)
notes: RD-002 CLOSED as untraced (COR-11.7). Never carried into the metrics table as history.

signal_or_failure: FAILED TRACING: the 1994 'roadmap' / 91-page notebook / 'Future of Computer Stores' planning document
what_it_demonstrated: That the founder DESCRIBED drafting a plan (rung 3): laptop 1997, prose-in-the-car 1999/2000, Excel 2013
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That any such document exists publicly or was ever read by an independent observer; the audited S-1 never mentions a planning document at all
notes: RD-009 resolved at rung 3; strings '91 pages', 'the roadmap', 'Future of Computer Stores' return zero hits across S-1, the FY1997 10-K and every cached file.

signal_or_failure: FAILED TRACING: the 'first sale' legend and its dates - 16 July 1995, or 3 April 1995 (Wainwright, $27.95), or 'a science textbook'
what_it_demonstrated: That the month July 1995 is audited, and that the only figure common to all variants is $27.95
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: The day, the customer and the title: no 1995-97 Amazon document names a first customer, title or day
confidence: High (that the legend is unresolved) / Low (on every specific)
notes: U.2; RD-001 and RD-012. MarketWatch 2015 and Atlantic 2012 are one interview cycle; the Atlantic piece prints both 3 April and the company's July dating.

signal_or_failure: FAILED TRACING: first-week sales of $12,000 and second-week $14,000, and the sentence 'shipped our first book in August 1995'
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing verifiable
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That they reconcile to anything: they are undated, Tier-2/3, and unreconcilable to a ship-basis audited year; the August sentence is absent from all five SEC documents searched
notes: COR-09. HistoryLink 2025 cites Stone 2013; one lineage, not corroboration.

signal_or_failure: FAILED TRACING: the Bulgarian order said to have been paid on a floppy disk
what_it_demonstrated: That the story circulates as a Stage-1 anecdote
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That it happened: the closest artifact is a 2005-retold payment failure and no 1995-97 record supports it
notes: Document named because no source_id resolves: The Seattle Times, 'Amazon at 10: Will it keep clicking?' published 2005-07-10, which is NOT registered in sources.csv. COR-09 lists this among figures that must never appear as Stage-1 fact.

signal_or_failure: REJECTED AS EVIDENCE: a hostile on-site order test reporting a 37-minute order and a 'confusing' order form
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing: the byline carries Stephen Glass's fabrication record
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the 1995-96 order flow was slow - the proposition is left untested rather than answered
notes: Excluded on provenance, not on outcome; a re-test of the same proposition remains open.

signal_or_failure: DOCUMENTED NULL: no Washington Post ownership or media stake, and no 'Post credibility' mechanism, is evidenced
what_it_demonstrated: That the principal-holder table lists only Bezos, KPCB vehicles (1996) and individual directors, with parents and sister at $0.1717-$0.3333
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any borrowing of institutional credibility in Stage 1: it is absent by record, not by inference
notes: COR-09: the Washington Post stake belongs in the retired-claims list.

signal_or_failure: UNSUPPORTED CHANNEL CLAIMS: no evidence that radio, television, search engines or paid media drove 1995 orders; customer gifts are undated and uncosted
what_it_demonstrated: That FY1995 marketing was $200,000 with only $30,000 of advertising, so paid acquisition was near-absent
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That any specific channel worked: referral share and word-of-mouth contribution were never measured in Stage 1
notes: 'Traffic came from search engines' is not evidenced; the S-1's word-of-mouth account is an asserted theory filed under penalty of perjury.

signal_or_failure: UNTRACEABLE MONEY STORY: '$1.1M from 22 friends and family at $50,000 each, ~20% for a ~$5M valuation'
magnitude: 23 purchasers, 3,021,000 shares, $1,007,000 as filed, window 1995-12-06 to 1996-05-16
what_it_demonstrated: That a disclosed round exists and is near the legend on magnitude
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the legend's structure is true: per-investor amounts, the roster of 23 and any 1995 valuation are not disclosed anywhere
notes: COR-10 and RD-003: only an undated part of the $1,007,000 programme closed inside Stage 1; the audited CY1995 headline is $1,272,000. Do not average the two.

signal_or_failure: DOCUMENTED NULL: no 1995 money-back, security or satisfaction guarantee language exists
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing in-window
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That customers had any stated protection: the first retrievable '100% secure - guaranteed' wording is on a 1999-08-28 capture
notes: COR-09: any 1995 guarantee claim is out of evidence; trust devices in 1995 were a published phone number (press release dated 1995-10-04), a toll-free line and nine e-mail addresses (S-1 (orig.), l.2179-2180 and l.2174) — COR-13: the release itself names neither the toll-free line nor the addresses.

signal_or_failure: The core selection claim rests on an unidentified third party: catalogue data was 'licensed ... from third parties' with the licensor unnamed
what_it_demonstrated: That the million-title offer was a listing over licensed data plus distributor files, not owned stock
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Who supplied the data: the Books-in-Print attribution rests on no retrieved document
notes: Ingram and Baker & Taylor are named as BOOK suppliers only, not as the bibliographic-data source.

signal_or_failure: FOUNDER-STATE GAP: no contemporaneous founder-state interview exists for Stage 1
what_it_demonstrated: That the 1995-10-04 press release carries a Bezos quotation dated inside the window
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: His reasoning: what exists is a publicity quotation and retrospective interviews conducted from 1999
notes: COR-06: Sheff self-dates to a 1999 interview published 2000; his genuine 1994 Wired profile of Bezos remains unfound (RD-013 closed with no contamination).

signal_or_failure: EVIDENCE DESTRUCTION AND RESTORATION: the shared evidence cache was destroyed mid-run; several load-bearing sources remain restoration-pending
